html:
Mandalay was founded in 1857 by King Mindon as the new royal capital of Burma, at the foot of Mandalay Hill on the Irrawaddy. Its square palace city, surrounded by a moat, was the last royal capital.

Mindon, who had lost Lower Burma to Britain, tried to modernise and to strengthen Buddhism. He hosted the Fifth Buddhist Council in Mandalay in 1871 and had the scriptures carved on hundreds of marble slabs.

British troops took the city in the Third Anglo-Burmese War of 1885. The palace burned in 1945 during the Burma campaign. Mandalay is now Burma's second city and a centre of monasteries and trade with China.
